newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem Steel sees relatively good demand.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem Steel sees relatively good demand.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp Tuesday reported sharply higher first quarter profits saying demand from steel users should continue to be relatively good.
The company's had net income of $38 million on sales of $1.19 billion in the latest quarter compared to $100,000 on sales of $1.12 billion a year earlier.

The company believes the domestic economy will continue on a course of moderate and sustainable growth and low inflation in 1997 and that the global economy will show some additional strength later this year.

Bethlehem said "the demand from the major steel-consuming sectors should continue to be relatively good and domestic industry steel shipments in 1997 should be close to the 100 million tons shipped in 1996.
"We recognize, however, that competition will remain intense in all of our markets as new steel production capacity and ... imports continue to enter the marketplace."
Noting plans announced in 1996 to exit several underperforming businesses, the company said it has ceased production at Bethlehem Structural and efforts to sell this business have been unsuccessful.
"We are proceeding with the sale of the structural assets. We are currently negotiating the sale of our BethForge, CENTEC and BethShip businesses."

The company said its Basic Steel Operations segment had income from operations of $64 million on shipments of 2,220,000 tons in the latest quarter compared to $21 million on shipments of 2,103,000 tons for the first quarter of 1996.
It said results improved from a year ago due to increased shipments, lower costs and higher average realized prices.

"We were able to increase shipments and lower costs compared to last year due to improved operating performance at Sparrows Point and Pennsylvania Steel Technologies, the elimination of operating problems at Bethlehem Structural and the absence of severe winter weather at Pennsylvania Steel Tecnologies and the work stoppage at General Motors.
"Additionally, depreciation expense was lower than a year ago principally due to the write-off of assets as part of our fourth quarter 1996 restructuring charge," Bethlehem said.
First quarter 1997 income from operations increased by $17 million from the fourth quarter of 1996 principally from higher shipments and lower costs, the company said.

Shipments of coated products to the automotive market increased at Burns Harbor, shipments of premium rail and pipe increased at PST and shipments of sheet piling were significantly higher at Bethlehem Structural in connection with its planned shutdown during the first quarter of 1997. Reduced repair and maintenance costs and higher yields, particularly at Sparrows Point, favorably impacted costs.

Cash provided from operating activities during the first quarter of 1997 was $68 million compared to $22 million in the first quarter of 1996. Principal uses of cash during the first quarter of 1997 included capital expenditures of $50 million, working capital of $44 million, debt repayments of $26 million and pension funding of $25 million.

During the first four months of this year, Bethlehem said, it made contributions of $145 million to its pension trust. "These contributions, along with additional contributions we plan to make during the year, should result in further reducing our pension expense and liability."

Bethlehem said the sale of its interest in Iron Ore Company of Canada to North Ltd resulted in cash proceeds about $145 million and an after-tax gain of $113 million, or $1.01 per share, which will be recorded in the second quarter.

The company said major uses of cash for 1997 include an estimated $280 million of capital expenditures, additional pension funding and repayment of approximately $50 million of debt and capital lease obligations.
